descriptor: Diversified investment holding company · ~26.25% fully-diluted look-through stake in Lenovo Group · reported in CNY · quoted in HKD

sections.title: Growth & Profitability
sections.subtitle: Consolidated accounts are ~92% Lenovo (33%-owned) plus BIL, a consolidated European bank; consolidated P/E, margins and FCF are not what this stock is valued on -- see the SOTP section below.

Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Reported consolidated FCF is dominated by BIL's customer-loan/deposit flows and Lenovo's working-capital swings; it is not the valuation base. Owner FCF (KPI above) is the DCF's 26.25% look-through share of Lenovo alone, post holdco discount.

sections.title: Sum-of-the-Parts NAV Bridge
sections.subtitle: Legend's worth is ~70% a listed Lenovo stake, ~15% a saleable Luxembourg bank, and the rest a mixed VC/PE and industrial portfolio, all behind holdco debt and a structural discount the market has applied for a decade.

charts.annotation: HK$/share, before the 60% holding-company discount. The same 60% is then applied proportionally in every scenario (see dcf.model_approach_note).

charts.annotation: Everything except the Lenovo look-through DCF. Lenovo itself (the dominant driver) is the owner-FCF chart above, not this bridge.

charts.annotation: Both figures are Legend's 26.25% fully-diluted interest in Lenovo. The DCF lands within ~7% of the market mark (dcf_vs_market_pct).

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Legend Holdings: consolidated equity is ~67% minority interest (Lenovo's other owners, BIL's 10%, Joyvio's 11%) -- Legend's own attributable share is the SOTP book value used in the NAV bridge below, not this consolidated line.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • The minority-interest share, which swamps Legend's own slice

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings on a consolidated basis.

For Legend Holdings: this consolidated figure mixes Lenovo's net-cash position, BIL's banking balance sheet, and Legend's own holdco borrowings (RMB30.5bn at the Company level). The DCF's net-debt line uses only Legend's 26.25% share of Lenovo's net cash ex in-the-money convertibles -- a much narrower number.

What to watch:

  • Holdco-level borrowings specifically (Company balance sheet note), since that debt sits ahead of every other asset in the bridge
  • BIL sale proceeds, which would de-lever the structure if the deal closes

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share.

For Legend Holdings: attributable net income has been negative or near zero in three of the last four years (FY2023: -RMB3,874m on VC marks) and no dividend was paid for FY2025 -- EPS here is not a reliable growth signal for a look-through holdco.

What to watch:

  • Warrant and convertible fair-value swings at the Lenovo level driving headline EPS noise
  • Whether a BIL sale restores the dividend

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is consolidated operating cash flow less capital expenditure.

For Legend Holdings: consolidated FCF swings from +RMB35bn (FY2020) to -RMB5.8bn (FY2023) on BIL's customer-loan and deposit flows and Lenovo's working capital -- no owner-FCF CAGR is meaningful at this level. The DCF instead builds Owner FCF bottom-up from Legend's 26.25% fully-diluted share of Lenovo's calendar-year segment figures, net of SBC, interest income and leases, then applies the 60% holding-company discount.

What to watch:

  • Consolidated FCF is a BIL/Lenovo statistic, not a Legend cash-return statistic
  • The Owner FCF KPI above, which is the actual DCF base

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin and net margin on the consolidated accounts.

For Legend Holdings: these are ~92% a Lenovo statistic (hardware assembly margins, mid-single-digit EBITDA) plus BIL's banking spread -- they say little about what Legend's own shareholders earn after minority interests and holdco costs.

What to watch:

  • Direction of the Lenovo-driven margin, not the level
  • One-off VC/PE marks distorting net margin in either direction

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets, both on a consolidated basis.

For Legend Holdings: consolidated OCF is dominated by BIL's banking flows (loans and deposits move through operating activities for a bank) and is not comparable to an industrial company's OCF/CapEx picture.

What to watch:

  • Lenovo's own capex intensity (~2.2% of its revenue), the only capex path the DCF actually projects

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit and net income on the consolidated accounts.

For Legend Holdings: net income is after ~67% minority interest (mostly Lenovo's other shareholders) is stripped out, so it understates the economic scale of the businesses Legend consolidates while still not isolating what the SOTP values.

What to watch:

  • Net income versus the attributable-equity trend (negative 3-5yr CAGR) -- growth at Lenovo has not reliably reached Legend's own bottom line

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the consolidated top line -- almost entirely Lenovo's (PCs, servers, AI infrastructure) plus BIL's banking income.

For Legend Holdings: the 3yr/5yr CAGR (~7.8%) is a Lenovo statistic used only as a PEG proxy; the DCF values Legend through Lenovo's own driver paths (AI-server scaling vs PC/memory cycle), not a blended consolidated growth rate.

What to watch:

  • Lenovo's AI-infrastructure mix (ISG) vs its legacy PC segment (IDG)
  • Whether consolidated growth is translating into attributable equity growth (it currently is not)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows Legend's own share count, which has been flat since 2018.

For Legend Holdings: Legend's own SBC is immaterial; the SBC in the DCF is Lenovo's (0.42% of Lenovo revenue), scaled to Legend's 26.25% look-through interest and expensed as a cash cost.

What to watch:

  • Legend's flat share count (no dilution at the holdco level)
  • Dilution instead happens at the Lenovo level -- convertibles and warrants, which is why the DCF uses the FULLY DILUTED 26.25% interest rather than the 32.95% headline stake

sotpNav.title: SOTP NAV per share by scenario
sotpNav.content:
The undiscounted NAV per share in each scenario, before the holding-company discount is applied. It is the Lenovo look-through DCF equity plus the equity bridge (BIL, Levima, Joyvio, portfolio), divided by Legend's 2,356.2m shares.

For Legend Holdings: only the Lenovo piece varies by scenario here (AI-server upside in bull, PC/memory-cycle downside in bear); the bridge items (BIL indication, Levima market price, Joyvio at zero, portfolio haircut) and the 60% discount are held constant across all three, so the bull case understates the upside available if the structural discount itself narrows (a move to 45% alone would add roughly HK$8/share).

What to watch:

  • Base case HK$56.56/share undiscounted vs HK$22.62 after the 60% discount -- the discount is the single biggest value driver on the page
  • Bear HK$35.87, bull HK$81.21: the spread is almost entirely the Lenovo EBITDA-margin and growth path

sotpBridge.title: SOTP bridge components (base case)
sotpBridge.content:
The non-Lenovo pieces of NAV, each at Legend's attributable share: BIL (Luxembourg bank, 89.98%, at the reported EUR2.5bn sale indication), Levima (advanced materials, 48.77%, at market), Joyvio (animal protein, 89.18%, written to zero), the investment portfolio less holdco net liabilities (a derived remainder of attributable book equity), a 25% haircut on that portfolio, and capitalised holdco corporate costs.

For Legend Holdings: BIL and Levima together are worth more than Joyvio, the portfolio haircut and corporate-cost capitalisation combined are negative -- the bridge is a net positive contributor to NAV, but a BIL sale falling through or a worse-than-25% portfolio mark are the two swing factors not driven by Lenovo at all.

What to watch:

  • BIL sale execution -- Luxembourg/ECB approval and final price vs the EUR2.5bn indication
  • Joyvio's debt load (~RMB12-13bn against ~RMB1.2bn of book equity) -- the zero mark assumes no further parent cash injections

lenovoCrossCheck.title: Lenovo look-through: DCF vs market
lenovoCrossCheck.content:
Legend's 26.25% fully-diluted look-through share of Lenovo, valued two ways: the DCF (owner-FCF, 9% WACC, scenario driver paths) versus Lenovo's own market price on the same diluted share count.

For Legend Holdings: the base-case DCF lands within ~7% of the market mark (dcf_vs_market_pct), which is the house's check that the model isn't making a Lenovo call the market disagrees with -- Lenovo is over 70% of Legend's NAV, so this single comparison matters more than any other chart on the page.

What to watch:

  • A DCF value far above the market mark would mean the model is betting against the market on Lenovo specifically
  • Both figures move with Lenovo's own share price and the CNY/HKD rate, independent of anything Legend-specific

dcf.base_sublabel: 26.25% fully-diluted Lenovo interest — after SBC, interest income & leases, post 60% holdco discount
dcf.model_approach_note: Sum-of-the-parts: owner-FCF DCF of Legend's fully diluted 26.25% look-through share of Lenovo (the only scenario-varying stream), plus BIL, Levima, Joyvio and the investment portfolio in an equity bridge at Legend's attributable share (sale indication, market, zero, and a haircut book remainder respectively), less capitalised holdco corporate costs, with a 60% holding-company discount applied proportionally across every flow and bridge item in every scenario. Precedent: 0087.HK (Swire Pacific) and 1113.HK (CK Asset).
